script.title: Pricing of material issues: FIFO vs LIFO
script.caption_hook: Same material, two lots, two prices. Which lot goes out first?

lines.say: Same material, two lots, different prices. Which lot goes out first?
Stores issue materials at the cost of a chosen lot. FIFO and LIFO choose the lot differently.
FIFO is a ticket queue: first in, first out. LIFO is a stack of plates: take the top one.
Say we buy 100 kg at ₹10, then 100 kg at ₹12. Now stores issue 150 kg.
FIFO: 100 kg at ₹10, then 50 kg at ₹12. Issue ₹1,600. Closing stock is 50 kg at ₹12, ₹600.
LIFO: latest lot in stock first. 100 kg at ₹12, then 50 kg at ₹10. Issue ₹1,700, closing stock ₹500.
But the totals differ. Did some money vanish?
No. Total cost is ₹2,200 either way. Only the split between issue and stock changes.
Can companies use LIFO for stock in financial statements?
AS 2 and Ind AS 2 don't permit LIFO for valuing inventory in financial statements. Cost records can still use it.

check_notes: Writer: The board has no stack icon, so the LIFO card uses chart_up (stacked bars) with the line saying "stack of plates". AS 2 (Revised) / Ind AS 2 wording follows the examiner's suggestion. Numbers: FIFO 1,600 + 600 = 2,200; LIFO 1,700 + 500 = 2,200. Word count is about 172 with the follow line.

Checker: Line 2 (voice): 'Stores issue materials at the cost of a chosen lot' is loose, because one issue can draw from more than one lot, as the 150 kg example does. Better: 'Stores price each issue from one or more lots, in an order set by the method. FIFO and LIFO follow a different order.'
Checker: Line 4 (board): the LIFO card uses the 'chart_up' icon, which doesn't fit the stack-of-plates comparison and could suggest rising prices. Use a stack or layers icon instead.
Checker: Line 8 (voice): 'But the totals differ' doesn't say which totals. Better: 'But the issue values differ, ₹1,600 and ₹1,700. Did some money vanish?'
